newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank group sees no big interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: German bank group sees no big interest rate rise.

text.p: The Bundesbank has no compelling reason to raise key interest rates significantly, as falling labour costs and slower money supply growth offset higher prices for imports, a German banking group said on Monday.

Despite market speculation of a rate increase to combat the weak mark, the central bank would be wrong to do more than raise the repo rate a few basis points, for stability reasons, the Association of German Banks (BDB) said in a regular report.

While rate-hike speculation has calmed in the past few days as the dollar retreated against the mark, a steepening of the yield curve on the German money market shows that such speculation has taken firm root, it said.
"Even if expectations of a slight rise in interest rates appear to have taken hold of financial markets, there is no need to fear a drastic change in interest rates at this time," the BDB said.

The Bundesbank may switch to variable-rate from fixed-rate repo tenders, resulting in a small rise in the repo rate, but low inflation and money supply growth argue against a need to raise other rates, it said.
